text:
tara: Hey team — planning to bump replicas for the analytics-api from 3 -> 5 for QPS headroom. Quick Qs before I open a PR: does anyone remember why we set `maxUnavailable: 25%` on the Deployment strategy? I'm worried rolling restarts are causing 503s for long-poll workers.

sam: I think that was historical to avoid surge during node pressure. But for this service we want zero downtime for short rolling windows. Can you paste the current strategy?

tara: Sure — current snippet from the manifest in k8s/overlays/prod/analytics-api.yaml:```yaml
strategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    maxSurge: 1
    maxUnavailable: 25%
```

maya: 25% on a 3-replica set means sometimes 1 pod down -> still okay, but during app startup the readiness probe takes ~20s so requests hit the remaining ones. If we go to 5 replicas maybe still fine, but +1 surge with `maxUnavailable: 0` is safer.

jon: Another option: set `maxSurge: 1` and `maxUnavailable: 0` so we always create the replacement before killing. Also make sure readiness probe is strict enough to avoid traffic before warmup.

tara: Thanks. Two infra/Terraform related questions: 1) Our k8s deployment is managed via Terraform module `kubernetes_deployment` in infra/apps. The variable is `replicas = var.analytics_replicas`. If I change the default from 3->5 and apply, will TF do a rolling update? 2) We also recently moved secrets to the CSI driver — will secret rotation trigger a restart?

sam: 1) Yes TF will patch the deployment.spec.replicas and Kubernetes will handle rolling update using the existing strategy. 2) CSI secret rotation only updates the projected volume contents; it doesn't restart pods by default unless the app watches file changes. So no implicit restart.

maya: If you want to force a rolling restart from TF (to pick up env changes), we usually add an annotation like `restartedAt` in `spec.template.metadata.annotations` with timestamp; TF can manage that.

tara: Pasting proposed TF change for infra/apps/analytics/main.tf:```hcl
module "analytics_deploy" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/infra-modules//k8s-deployment?ref=v2"
  name   = "analytics-api"
  replicas = 5
  image  = var.analytics_image
  annotations = {
    "rolling-strategy" = "maxSurge=1,maxUnavailable=0"
  }
}
```Would we prefer to encode `maxSurge`/`maxUnavailable` in the module instead?

jon: Prefer module defaults for safety. Add optional inputs `strategy_max_surge` and `strategy_max_unavailable` with sane defaults, then set them in the environment overlay. That avoids manual manifest edits across clusters.

sam: Also flag: CI pipeline will run `terraform plan` in PR. We should ensure the plan doesn't try to recreate the deployment resource (it shouldn't).

deploy-bot: CI check: terraform/analytics-pr-#421 — plan completed with 1 change: update `module.analytics_deploy.replicas` (3 -> 5). No resource replacement detected. :white_check_mark:

tara: Cool. One last concern: the service has a PDB set to `minAvailable: 2`. With 5 replicas that's fine, but if cluster autoscaler drains nodes we'll still be fine?

maya: PDB minAvailable=2 is OK but for zero downtime you might raise to 3. But beware during node upgrades if the cluster can't keep that many schedulable pods. I'd suggest `minAvailable: 2` for prod, `3` for higher SLA.

tara: OK I'll: 1) open a PR that bumps the TF var to 5, 2) add module inputs for strategy (defaults `maxSurge=1`, `maxUnavailable=0`), 3) add `spec.template.metadata.annotations.restartedAt` pattern commented for manual restarts, and 4) call out PDB change as optional in the PR description.

sam: SGTM. @jon can you do a quick review on the module input naming?

jon: On it. Expect comments in ~30m.

infra-bot: Note: scheduled cluster maintenance tonight 02:00 UTC — may cause transient reschedules. If PR merges before that, consider delaying rollout to avoid coinciding with maintenance.

tara: Good catch. I'll hold merge until after maintenance window. Thanks all :thumbsup:
